latest_release.name: v1.12.0
latest_release.body:
## Pro highlights

These features are in [It's a Plan Pro](https://itsaplan.dev/pro).

### Asana import

Import a project from Asana, with its tasks and subtasks, sections, tags, custom fields, comments, dependencies, time entries, and files. Sections or a single-select field such as Status become the columns, and people are matched by email or by name.

### More events in the audit log

The audit log records refused sign-ins of every method with the reason, apps connected over OAuth such as MCP clients, and profile changes. It also records changes to labels, public links, archived documents and initiatives, and four instance settings.

## Community highlights

### Color themes

Each account picks a color palette next to the light, dark, or system theme: Default, GitHub, Nord, Catppuccin, One, Tomorrow, or Nightfox. A custom palette is built from an accent, a background, and a contrast.

### Comment reactions

Add emoji reactions to issue comments. Hover a reaction to see who added it. The comment's author can get a notification, which is off until they turn it on.

### Agent runs in the background from the API and MCP

`run_ai_agent` and the API run route queue the run and answer at once with its id. The `get_agent_run` MCP tool reads the result when the run ends.

### Gitea and Forgejo pull requests

The Development panel of an issue works with Gitea and Forgejo as it does with GitHub and GitLab. Link a pull request or create one from a branch, a draft included.

### Kie and DataForSEO tools for agents

With a [Kie](https://kie.ai?ref=0b6eb19939298accdf58e18b1a92a26e) key, agents generate images, video, music, and speech with models such as Nano Banana, Kling, Veo, Suno, and ElevenLabs. With [DataForSEO](https://try.dataforseo.com/49wtthgg2yk6), agents read search results, keyword data, backlinks, and an SEO check of a page.

### MCP catalog mode

`/mcp?tools=catalog` lists 13 tools instead of 236: the most used ones, `discover`, and three tools that run any other tool. The tool list then takes about 4,000 tokens instead of about 150,000. Without the parameter nothing changes.

## Security

This release updates dependencies with published advisories.

- Dependencies: Next.js 16.4.6 fixes [GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8) and [GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mfr8-8qww-v76h) (medium). Both affect `'use cache'` functions, which the web app does not use. `hono`, `@hono/node-server`, `qs`, and `uuid` are updated to patched versions.

## Also in this release

- In Pro, a license key works on one instance. Another instance that uses the key gets a temporary license for 7 days, and the License page says how to make it the main instance.
- In Pro, an agent run started through the API or MCP counts toward the budget and the usage of the person who sent it.
- In Pro, a workflow step shows its tool calls folded, one row per call, and each opens to its request and response.
- In Pro, an HTTP connection can have a check path, so Check credential can test its key.
- The Agent runs page filters failed and running runs, has a search, and groups runs by day. A run opens with its result, its steps with their timings, and each attempt.
- God mode → General → API keys sets the API key rate limit, 1,200 requests a minute by default. Over the limit, REST and MCP answer 429 with `Retry-After`. The sign-in rate limits are on God mode → Authentication.
- God mode → General → Agents sets how many characters of an agent's answer are saved: 200,000 by default.
- Dashboard widgets are dragged onto the grid from a side panel.
- The board, table, and calendar views are cleaner, and the timelines follow right-to-left languages.
- The Persian timeline and calendar show Jalali days.
- An unsent comment is kept as a draft and comes back when you open the issue again.
- MCP tool descriptions are shorter, and `discover` understands everyday wor

# The open-source Linear alternative
where AI agents take issues like teammates Use it as a regular issue tracker from day one. When you are ready, give an agent an issue the way you give it to a colleague, and review the result yourself or let another agent check it. Put agents on a schedule, or build a workflow that passes an issue from agent to agent. Self-hosted, on your own server. If It's a Plan looks useful to you, star the repo ⭐ and [leave a review on Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/it-s-a-plan/reviews).
## Why It's a Plan - **Agents as project members.** Each gets a role, permissions and an assignee slot, and works on the same board as your people. - **Two kinds of agents.** Internal agents run on your server, on any model with your API key. External agents run on your machine through [`@itsaplan/runner`](packages/runner), under your own Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI or opencode account. - **Any kind of work.** Software, marketing, design, support, sales, operations, research. - **Yours to run.** Your server and your database. ## Community features | Area | What you get | | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Product management | Kanban, table, timeline, and calendar views · cycles · custom fields · dashboards · docs · notes boards · project templates · import from Linear, Trello, and Plane | | AI agents | Agents as project members · internal on any model, or external on your coding CLI · runs start on an @mention, an assignment, or a schedule | | Platform | REST API with OpenAPI · MCP server · webhooks · pull requests from 5 forges · SSO over OIDC and SCIM · passkeys and Google sign-in | | 13 languages | English · Українська · Русский · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · العربية · Français · فارسی · Português (Brasil) · Bahasa Indonesia · Español · 한국어 · Türkçe |
Product management: the full list - Configure issues per project: custom fields, labels, states, and issue types - Kanban, table, timeline, and calendar views. Save a view as a tab with its own filters, fields, and two-level grouping, for the whole project or only for you. Each person orders and hides their own tabs - Cycles that time-box the work. Unfinished issues move to the next cycle - Subtasks, checklists, attachments, and links between issues: blocks, relates, duplicates - Comment threads with replies, and @mentions of people and agents - Project dashboards: throughput, burnup with a projected completion date, breakdown, and pulse - Quick actions on an issue, and automatic assignment when an issue moves to a state - Docs: Markdown pages in a tree, with revision history, private and locked pages, embedded files, comments, @mentions, and links to issues - Notes boards: sticky notes on a canvas, with colors, checklists, and connections - Share a view, an issue, or a document by public link, read-only and without sign-in - Initiatives that group and track related work inside a project - Project templates: save a project as a template for your team, or publish it to the gallery at itsaplan.dev - Import projects from [Linear](docs/importing-from-linear.md), [Trello](docs/importing-from-trello.md), and [Plane](docs/importing-from-plane.md) - Auto-archive, a notification inbox, and role-based access control
AI agents: the full list - Agents as project members, with their own permissions and assigned issues - Internal agents run on the instance. Configure the model, system prompt, tools, and reusable skills, written inline or imported from a GitHub repository - External agents run on your machine, under your own account. [`@itsaplan/runner`](packages/runner) gives each task to Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, opencode, Pi, Oh My Pi, Mastra Code, or any command that reads stdin - Your own code can also take tasks from the run queue through the API - A run starts on an @mention in a comment on an issue or a document, on an assignment, or on a schedule. A schedule starts on a timer or when an issue moves to a state - Tokens and cost of every run, by agent, project, and model - Tools for other services: Notion, Baserow, Telegram, Threads, Instagram, Jina, Firecrawl, Keenable, DataForSEO, Gitea, Forgejo, and GitHub - Images, video, music, and speech from the models on [Kie](https://kie.ai?ref=0b6eb19939298accdf58e18b1a92a26e): Nano Banana, Seedream, Kling, Veo, Suno, and others, with one API key - Chat with each agent, with its own history. Turn chat off for an agent that only works on mentions, assignments, and schedules - Chat with an external agent too. The runner answers from your machine, streams the reply and its tool calls, and resumes the same coding agent session on each message
Platform: the full list - REST API with an OpenAPI reference and API keys - MCP server, so an external assistant can read and change issues through the same API - Pull requests from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, and Bitbucket. "Fixes KEY-42" links the pull request to the issue, and the issue moves when the pull request opens and merges - Outgoing webhooks for the events you pick, with signed payloads, retries, and a delivery log - Sign-in with an email or username and a password, a passkey, Google, or your identity provider over OIDC. SCIM keeps accounts in sync with your directory - Notifications by email (SMTP, Resend, or Microsoft 365) and Telegram, with preferences for each member - Instance administration: storage limits, the mail provider, and instance-wide settings
## Pro edition Bring the whole team. Pro adds full control over workspaces, agents and spend. > [!TIP] > **$240 a year for the whole instance, 1 person or 500.** Fast Deploy installs Pro on your own > server in about 5 minutes. Everything in Community, plus: - Fast Deploy - Unlimited workspaces - SAML or OIDC per workspace - SCIM per workspace - Workspace dashboard - Audit log - Agent workflows - Schedules on issue events - Agent cost by person, trigger and workflow - AI budgets - Public forms [See what each feature does →](https://itsaplan.dev/pro) Three ways to run Pro: - **[Fast Deploy](https://itsaplan.dev/pro#fast-deploy)** installs Pro on your own Hetzner, Vultr or DigitalOcean server in about 5 minutes. Updates take one click. - **[Railway](docs/railway.md):** the template runs Pro in one click. - **By hand:** deploy on [Docker](docs/self-hosting.md), [Coolify](docs/coolify.md) or [Kubernetes](docs/helm.md). On Railway and by hand, enter the key in god mode under **License**. Without a valid key, Pro runs as Community. Your data stays when you switch editions. ## Getting started ### Deploy on Railway — recommended [![Deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/button.svg)](https://railway.com/deploy/its-a-plan?referralCode=lQ5O6i&utm_medium=integration&utm_source=button&utm_campaign=itsaplan) The whole stack in one click, with no server to maintain. You give Railway two hostnames, and it generates every secret. You need a domain of your own: [the guide](docs/railway.md) explains why, and what to do after the deploy. ### Fast Deploy for Pro With a Pro license, [Fast Deploy](https://itsaplan.dev/account/hosting) installs Pro on a new server in your Hetzner, Vultr or DigitalOcean account. See [Pro edition](#pro-edition). ### Try it on your machine Requirements: Docker and [Bun](https://bun.sh). ```bash git clone https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan.git cd itsaplan bun install bun run setup # answer "Try it" ``` It picks free ports, generates the secrets, starts the whole stack in Docker, and opens . Everything runs on localhost, so no domain and no reverse proxy are needed. Run it again later to restart the instance; the data stays. ### Everything else - [Deploy on Railway](docs/railway.md) — one-click hosted deploy from the template - [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md) — the full production setup, secrets, and updates - [Deploy on Coolify](docs/coolify.md) — the same stack on a Coolify instance - [Deploy on Kubernetes](docs/helm.md) — Helm chart for any Kubernetes cluster - [Local development](docs/development.md) — running the apps on the host, and the tests - [Coding agent setup](docs/runner.md) — the config for each CLI that `@itsaplan/runner` runs - [Agent endpoint](docs/agent-endpoint.md) — the instance sends an external agent's tasks to a URL that you run, such as an AWS Lambda function ## Built with | Layer | Technology | | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Runtime | [Bun](https://bun.sh) + [Turborepo](https://turbo.build) | | Backend | [Elysia](https://elysiajs.com/) | | Frontend | [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) App Router, SSR | | UI | [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) + Tailwind v4 | | Auth | [better-auth](https://better-auth.com/) | | Database | [Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team/) + PostgreSQL | | Storage | S3-compatible object store (RustFS) | | AI agents | [Mastra](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra) | ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — bug fixes, features, docs, all of it. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). It covers the setup, the conventions, and how a change gets merged. Be kind; we follow a [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Thank you to everyone who has contributed to It's a Plan: Not ready to contribute code? [Star the repo](https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan) and share it — it is the simplest way to help the project grow. ## Security Found a vulnerability? Report it privately through [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/croffasia/itsaplan/security/advisories/new), not a public issue, so we can fix it first. Details in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License Copyright © 2026 Andrii Poluosmak. [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE), except `packages/runner`, which is [Apache-2.0](packages/runner/LICENSE). A commercial licence is available if AGPL-3.0 does not fit your company. Ask on [Telegram](https://telegram.me/croffasia).
